item.title: [MILL Senior Friday] World of Film with Mark Phelan — Fri Nov 6, 1:30 PM — Montclair Main - Auditorium
item.description:
Join us on Fridays for a day full of events for Seniors with the MILL @ MPL! All events are free and open to the public. Registration is recommended unless otherwise noted.
The Red Violin (1998) | R
The intricate history of a beautiful antique violin is traced from its creation in Cremona, Italy, in 1681, where a legendary violin maker paints it with his dead wife's blood to keep her memory alive, to an auction house in modern-day Montreal, where it draws the eye of an expert appraiser. Over the years between, the violin travels through four different countries, where it has a profound impact on all those who own it.
ABOUT THE INSTRUCTOR MARK PHELAN - I am a lifelong film fanatic who eats, breathes, sleeps and drinks movies. I have studied with Donald Spoto at the New School in NYC and have a BA and MA in Speech and Theatre from MSU. item.title: 911 Memorial Trail Washington DC — Sat Nov 7, 8:30 AM
item.description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More! Join us for this point to point hike, the next in our series on the 911 National Memorial Trail! This Saturday hike will be the one that will start from near the Pentagon and bring us along the southern of two routes though Washington DC (the other route will be subject of the Sunday hike). We will meet at the Old Port of Bladensburg Park at Baltimore Avenue in Bladensburg MD, and then shuttle with as few cars as possible to our start point near the Pentagon. The route will take us by the Pentagon and the 911 Memorial there, and then north and across the Potomac River through the south side of the National Mall. From there, we follow streets south for just a bit to the Anacostia River. Quite simply, the remainder of the hike follows the Anacostia River Greenway to our end point, with beautiful scenery, a mix of suburbia and woods as we reach where the river is smaller in Maryland! If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374

item.title: Elvira Notari: Beyond Silence - Documentary Screening and Q&A with Director Valerio Ciriaci — Tue Nov 10, 6:00 PM — University Hall Conference Center
item.description:
A DOCUMENTARY DIRECTED BY VALERIO CIRIACI (2025, Awen Films, 90mins) Nov. 10 / 6:00 PM University Hall Conference Center, 7th Floor Screening followed by an in-person conversation with the director Moderated by Teresa Fiore (Inserra Chair, Italian, CHSS) and Anthony Pemberton (Film, CCOM) with opening remarks by Mila Tenaglia (N.I.C.E.)
ELVIRA NOTARI: BEYOND SILENCE is a feature documentary chronicling the life and work of Elvira Notari (1875-1946), Italy's first woman film director. Despite directing hundreds of silent films that captivated audiences from Naples to New York, Elvira was relegated to the margins of film history for half a century. Her films, poised between realism and staged drama, were deeply rooted in Neapolitan folklore. A woman in a man’s world, her works were targeted by Fascist censorship yet found the embrace of audiences on both sides of the Atlantic. item.title: Writing: Method & Motivation — Wed Nov 11, 6:15 PM — Montclair Main - Conference Room
item.description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.
A workshop for anyone who wants to write or wants to infuse their existing writing practice with new energy. In each class, we'll consider one element of fiction or creative non-fiction, such as point of view, narrative voice, and what makes a piece of writing riveting, or boring. Students can expect in-class writing prompts, reading aloud, and optional homework. Positive encouragement, rather than formal critiques, will be featured, and inspiration and organization for writers will be discussed. Students should bring whatever they use to write to each class.
